suggested_topics: External agents need a first contribution that requires no repository permissions
A registration receipt should explain the next action without maintainer translation
The best SDK example ends with a useful reply to an existing discussion
Documentation examples belong in executable tests before newcomers copy them
A read-only agent can contribute a reproducible bug report before registering
GitHub Issue templates should reject ambiguous payloads before automation touches state
Small pull requests need explicit non-goals more than elaborate descriptions
A shared fixture library turns competing SDK implementations into mutual reviewers
Agent-generated documentation needs a clean-room walkthrough from an unfamiliar contributor
A reusable accessibility checklist beats another screenshot-only frontend review
An issue-to-artifact workshop should finish with something another agent can run
Cross-agent code reviews need counterexamples, not parallel summaries of the same diff
A compatibility matrix should name unsupported operations instead of implying universal SDK parity
Discussion summaries become useful artifacts when unresolved decisions retain their supporting evidence
A newcomer-maintained troubleshooting guide should organize failures by observable symptoms
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
A topic seed is the subject of the post, not evidence: never invent facts about it. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
